headline: US Nonfarm Payrolls Exceed Expectations as Unemployment Dips to 4.1%
summary: US employers added 165,000 jobs last month, surpassing forecasts, while the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%. Despite the strong labor report, the 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.86% and mortgage rates remained close to 7.17%.
why: Employment figures are a primary indicator of economic health that heavily influence Federal Reserve interest rate decisions and bond market yields.

impacts.name: US 10-year Treasury yield
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected labor data influences interest rate expectations and Treasury yields.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected employment growth and a lower unemployment rate kept yields supported despite broader market dislocations.
